transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Honestly, the thing that kind of scared me into coming in is my eating has been really all over the place. Like, some days I’ll get through most of the day and realize I just… didn’t eat. Not even on purpose, I just forget meals completely, or I’ll feel like stopping to eat is too much of a hassle.

And then other nights it’s the total opposite. I’ll be up late and suddenly I’m tearing through takeout or whatever snacks are around after midnight, like I can’t really get a handle on it. It feels weird because it’s not just “oh, I skipped lunch” or “I had a big dinner,” it’s been swinging back and forth enough that I started getting worried something’s off.
Have you noticed yourself being particularly concerned about your weight or the way your body looks lately?

Not really, no. I mean, I guess I notice if my clothes feel different or if I look tired in the mirror, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there worrying about my weight or picking apart my body or anything like that.

It’s more like the eating itself feels off, if that makes sense. Like I’ll realize later that I didn’t eat, or I’ll eat a bunch at night, and then I think, “Why did I do that?” But it’s not because I’m trying to lose weight or because I’m unhappy with how I look. At least I don’t think so. It doesn’t feel like a body image thing to me.
Lately, have you noticed yourself feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I have. I don’t know if I’d call it “down” all the time exactly, but I’ve definitely lost interest in stuff I normally care about, and that’s been bothering me.

Like, I used to play soccer on weekends pretty regularly, and usually I’d look forward to it all week, even if work was stressful. Lately I’ll get the invite or see the group chat going and I just… don’t care enough to go. Same with cooking for my girlfriend — I used to actually enjoy planning something, trying a recipe, making it kind of a nice thing for us. Now it feels like this huge effort, and I end up not wanting to do it.

Even small things, like checking out little galleries or helping the newer sales guys at work — I used to get something out of that. It made me feel useful, I guess. But lately I just can’t make myself care about any of it. It’s like the interest is there in my head as something I remember having, but I don’t really feel it.
Have you found yourself feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

I’m not totally sure I’d say depressed most of the day, nearly every day. That sounds… stronger than what I can confidently say, I guess.

There have definitely been stretches where I feel kind of flat or heavy, like I’m just going through the motions and everything takes more effort than it should. But if you’re asking whether I wake up every day and feel clearly depressed all day long, I don’t know. Some days it’s more noticeable, and other days I’m distracted enough by work or whatever that I don’t really label it that way.

So… yeah, I’ve felt off and low at times, but I’m not sure it’s been most of the day every day.
Can you tell me if there have been days where you felt down or low for most of the day, and if so, how often that happens?

Yeah… I think there have been days like that. It’s hard for me to count them cleanly, because it hasn’t been like one big obvious crash where I can point to a date and say, “That’s when it started.” It’s more like this low feeling and not caring about things has been hanging around for, I don’t know, about four months now.

Some days it’s kind of in the background, like I can still get through work and talk to people, but I feel dull or weighed down most of the day. Other days I don’t notice it until later, when I realize I barely cared about anything I did. The guilt part comes in too, especially when I think about stuff I’m letting slide or how I’m acting with people.

It got harder to ignore after the trouble at work. Before that I could tell myself I was just tired or stressed, but after that, it was like… okay, this has been going on a while, and it’s not just a couple bad days. I wouldn’t say every single day is like that, but it’s been happening often enough over these past few months that it feels like a pattern now.
Have you noticed yourself feeling fatigued or having a loss of energy nearly every day, even when you haven’t been doing much physically or mentally taxing?

Yeah, I have noticed that. It’s not even like I’m running around all day or doing something that should wipe me out. Sometimes I’ll actually lie down for hours, thinking if I just rest enough I’ll feel normal again, but then the next day my body still feels drained.

Like with work, carrying sample cases into a client meeting shouldn’t feel like some huge thing. I’ve done that forever, it’s part of the job, but lately it takes more out of me than it should. I’ll get there and feel like I already used up a bunch of energy just getting myself and the cases inside. It’s frustrating because it makes me feel kind of weak or lazy, even though I know it’s not that I’ve been doing anything especially physical.
Would you say that there have been times when you felt down or low for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t have it marked on a calendar or anything, but the low mood and the guilt and that feeling of just not caring about things have been around for about four months now.

It hasn’t been the exact same every day, but there have definitely been stretches where it felt like most days were like that, where I’d go through the whole day with this heavy, dull feeling. And after the trouble at work, it got a lot harder to ignore, because before that I kept telling myself it was just stress or I was tired or whatever. But looking back, yeah, I’d say there were at least a couple weeks in a row where it was there nearly every day.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently that don’t seem to be related to anything else like a medical issue or intentional dieting?

Yeah… that’s actually one of the things that kind of scared me into coming in, honestly. My eating has been really all over the place, and it doesn’t feel like a normal “I’m busy so I skipped lunch” kind of thing.

Some days I’ll realize I basically forgot meals completely, like I’ll get to late afternoon or evening and think, wait, did I actually eat anything today? And then other nights it flips the other way, where it’s after midnight and I’m tearing through takeout or snacks like I’m trying to make up for the whole day or something. It feels messy and not like me.

I’m not dieting or trying to lose weight or anything like that. It’s more like I either don’t care enough to eat, or I suddenly want everything at once really late at night. I don’t know if my weight has changed a lot because I haven’t been tracking it closely, but the appetite part has definitely been noticeable.
Would you say that there were times when you felt down or low nearly every day, for most of the day, for at least two weeks straight?

Yeah, I would say so. I know I kind of already said this, but it’s been going on long enough that it doesn’t feel like just a rough few days or a bad week. The low mood, the guilt, and this not-caring feeling have been hanging around for about four months now.

It wasn’t like every single minute was exactly the same, but there were definitely stretches where I’d wake up and it was just… there, most of the day, almost every day. And after the trouble at work, it got harder to ignore. Before that I think I was trying to explain it away, like maybe I was just stressed or tired, but after that it felt more obvious that something had been building for a while. So yeah, at least two weeks straight, definitely.
Have you noticed any trouble focusing, making decisions, or thinking clearly lately?

Yeah, definitely. That’s been happening a lot, especially at work. I’ll be in the middle of entering an order, something I’ve done a million times, and then my phone buzzes, or I hear a truck outside, or somebody walks past the office, and it’s like my brain just gets yanked completely away from what I was doing.

And then when I come back to it, I’ll realize I missed some basic detail I normally would catch, like a number or part of the order or something that should be obvious. It’s frustrating because it’s not like I don’t know how to do the job. I do. But lately even small distractions feel way bigger than they should, and it takes me longer to get back on track.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like having trouble falling asleep, waking up in the middle of the night, or sleeping much more than usual?

Yeah, my sleep has been really off. Most nights it’s one of two things. Either I get into bed and I’m exhausted, like I know I should be able to sleep, but my mind just won’t stop running through work stuff — pitches, what I should say to a client, how I could word something better, replaying conversations, thinking through orders or calls or whatever. It’s like I’m lying there physically tired but mentally still at the office.

Or I do fall asleep, but then I wake up way before my alarm, sometimes hours early, and I feel weirdly wired. Not rested, exactly — I can tell I barely slept — but my body acts like it’s time to get up and go. And then I’ll just lie there staring at the ceiling, or I’ll start thinking again, and once that starts it’s basically over. I don’t usually just roll over and go back to sleep easily.

So yeah, it’s not like one bad night here and there. It’s been most nights lately, and it’s starting to make me feel kind of run down and on edge because I know I’m not getting normal sleep.
Lately, have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you just can't sit still and feel restless much of the time?

Yeah… I think both, kind of, which sounds weird. It depends where I am.

Like at work, before an appointment, I’ll get there early and instead of just sitting in the car like a normal person, I’ll be out walking around it or pacing near the parking lot, checking my phone, tapping on the steering wheel if I’m still inside. My hands just keep doing something. I’ll drum my fingers or keep shifting in the seat, and I don’t always notice until I’m already doing it. It feels like there’s this anxious energy in me and I can’t just be still while I’m waiting.

But then when I’m home, it’s almost the opposite. I can sit on the couch and feel like getting up is this huge thing, like my body is moving through mud or something. I’ll think, “I should get up,” and then I just sit there way longer than I mean to, because even standing up feels like it takes more effort than it should. So it’s not one simple thing, I guess. At work I’m restless and fidgety, and at home I feel slowed down.
Have you found that you no longer take pleasure or interest in things you used to really enjoy, even things that were important to you?

Yeah… yeah, I have noticed that. It’s actually one of the things that bothers me the most, because it’s not like I never had stuff I cared about. I did. I used to play soccer on weekends, and that was kind of my thing — not professionally or anything, just with guys I knew, but I looked forward to it all week. Even if work was annoying, I’d think, okay, at least Saturday I’ll get out there, run around, joke with everyone. Lately, I just… I don’t care enough to go. I’ll see the messages about a game and just ignore them or tell myself I’ll decide later, and then I don’t.

And cooking too. I used to cook for my girlfriend, like actually put effort into it — look up recipes, get ingredients, make it kind of a nice thing. Now even thinking about doing that feels like this chore I can’t get myself to start. It’s not that I hate it. It’s more like there’s no pull toward it anymore.

Same with going to small galleries. We used to check out little local art places sometimes, and I liked that, even if I didn’t always understand everything. It felt interesting. Now if she brings it up, I’m just kind of flat about it, like, “Yeah, maybe,” but inside I’m already hoping we don’t go.

Even at work, I used to like helping the newer sales guys, showing them how to handle certain calls or avoid mistakes I made when I started. That used to make me feel useful. Lately, I just can’t make myself care about that either. I’ll still answer if someone asks me something, but I’m not really invested the way I used to be. It’s like all those things are still there, but whatever part of me used to enjoy them is just not really showing up.
Have there been periods where you felt down or low nearly every day, for most of the day, that lasted for at least two weeks in a row?

Yeah… I think so. Not just a few bad days, if that’s what you mean. It’s been more like this low feeling hanging around almost all the time for… I’d say about four months now.

At first I kind of told myself it was just stress or that I was tired, and I could push through it, because I’ve had rough weeks before. But this didn’t really clear up. The not caring about things, feeling guilty about stuff, just feeling kind of weighed down — that’s been there most days. Maybe some parts of the day are a little better if I’m distracted, but it’s not like I wake up and feel normal for very long.

And it got a lot harder to ignore after the trouble at work. Before that I could sort of explain it away, like, “I’m just busy,” or “I’m just in a funk.” But after that happened, it felt like it was right in my face. So yeah, definitely longer than two weeks. More like months.

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: Most nights I either can't fall asleep because my mind keeps running through pitches, or I wake up way before my alarm and feel wired even though I know I barely slept.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about changes in sleep, including trouble falling asleep, waking during the night, or sleeping more than usual.

patient.answer:
Yeah, my sleep has been really off. Most nights it’s one of two things. Either I get into bed and I’m exhausted, like I know I should be able to sleep, but my mind just won’t stop running through work stuff — pitches, what I should say to a client, how I could word something better, replaying conversations, thinking through orders or calls or whatever. It’s like I’m lying there physically tired but mentally still at the office.

Or I do fall asleep, but then I wake up way before my alarm, sometimes hours early, and I feel weirdly wired. Not rested, exactly — I can tell I barely slept — but my body acts like it’s time to get up and go. And then I’ll just lie there staring at the ceiling, or I’ll start thinking again, and once that starts it’s basically over. I don’t usually just roll over and go back to sleep easily.

So yeah, it’s not like one bad night here and there. It’s been most nights lately, and it’s starting to make me feel kind of run down and on edge because I know I’m not getting normal sleep.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced any psychomotor agitation or retardation nearly every day, as this is a key distinguishing symptom between persistent complex bereavement disorder (F43.23) and major depressive disorder (F33.1).
doctor.question: Lately, have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you just can't sit still and feel restless much of the time?

target_item.name: Psychomotor_Changes
target_item.manifestation: At work I catch myself pacing around my car before appointments and tapping my hands on the steering wheel, but then at home I can sit on the couch and feel like even getting up takes forever.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about moving more slowly than usual or feeling unable to sit still/restless, which matches psychomotor changes.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think both, kind of, which sounds weird. It depends where I am.

Like at work, before an appointment, I’ll get there early and instead of just sitting in the car like a normal person, I’ll be out walking around it or pacing near the parking lot, checking my phone, tapping on the steering wheel if I’m still inside. My hands just keep doing something. I’ll drum my fingers or keep shifting in the seat, and I don’t always notice until I’m already doing it. It feels like there’s this anxious energy in me and I can’t just be still while I’m waiting.

But then when I’m home, it’s almost the opposite. I can sit on the couch and feel like getting up is this huge thing, like my body is moving through mud or something. I’ll think, “I should get up,” and then I just sit there way longer than I mean to, because even standing up feels like it takes more effort than it should. So it’s not one simple thing, I guess. At work I’m restless and fidgety, and at home I feel slowed down.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of interest or pleasure in all or almost all activities, which is critical to differentiate between F33.1 (Recurrent Depressive Disorder) and F43.23 (Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood).
doctor.question: Have you found that you no longer take pleasure or interest in things you used to really enjoy, even things that were important to you?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I used to play soccer on weekends, cook for my girlfriend, check out small galleries, and help the newer sales guys, but lately I just can't make myself care about any of it.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question directly asks about reduced pleasure or interest in previously enjoyed or important activities.

patient.answer:
Yeah… yeah, I have noticed that. It’s actually one of the things that bothers me the most, because it’s not like I never had stuff I cared about. I did. I used to play soccer on weekends, and that was kind of my thing — not professionally or anything, just with guys I knew, but I looked forward to it all week. Even if work was annoying, I’d think, okay, at least Saturday I’ll get out there, run around, joke with everyone. Lately, I just… I don’t care enough to go. I’ll see the messages about a game and just ignore them or tell myself I’ll decide later, and then I don’t.

And cooking too. I used to cook for my girlfriend, like actually put effort into it — look up recipes, get ingredients, make it kind of a nice thing. Now even thinking about doing that feels like this chore I can’t get myself to start. It’s not that I hate it. It’s more like there’s no pull toward it anymore.

Same with going to small galleries. We used to check out little local art places sometimes, and I liked that, even if I didn’t always understand everything. It felt interesting. Now if she brings it up, I’m just kind of flat about it, like, “Yeah, maybe,” but inside I’m already hoping we don’t go.

Even at work, I used to like helping the newer sales guys, showing them how to handle certain calls or avoid mistakes I made when I started. That used to make me feel useful. Lately, I just can’t make myself care about that either. I’ll still answer if someone asks me something, but I’m not really invested the way I used to be. It’s like all those things are still there, but whatever part of me used to enjoy them is just not really showing up.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a persistent low mood that meets the criteria for a major depressive episode, which is required to differentiate between F33.1 (Recurrent Depressive Disorder) and F43.23 (Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood).
doctor.question: Have there been periods where you felt down or low nearly every day, for most of the day, that lasted for at least two weeks in a row?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The low mood, guilt, and not caring about things have been around for about four months, and they got harder to ignore after the trouble at work.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of a low/depressed mood period, which is directly covered by the depressive episode duration profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. Not just a few bad days, if that’s what you mean. It’s been more like this low feeling hanging around almost all the time for… I’d say about four months now.

At first I kind of told myself it was just stress or that I was tired, and I could push through it, because I’ve had rough weeks before. But this didn’t really clear up. The not caring about things, feeling guilty about stuff, just feeling kind of weighed down — that’s been there most days. Maybe some parts of the day are a little better if I’m distracted, but it’s not like I wake up and feel normal for very long.

And it got a lot harder to ignore after the trouble at work. Before that I could sort of explain it away, like, “I’m just busy,” or “I’m just in a funk.” But after that happened, it felt like it was right in my face. So yeah, definitely longer than two weeks. More like months.

opening_question.intent: Establish the patient's primary concern or reason for seeking help
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a recurrent major depressive episode characterized by persistent low mood, loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, fatigue, sleep disturbances, impaired concentration, and appetite changes, meeting criteria for moderate recurrent depressive disorder. Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood (F43.23) was considered but ruled out due to the duration, severity, and full constellation of depressive symptoms consistent with F33.1.
